images.title: A frame of 16 tiles
images.purpose: Shows Step 3 of the tile pattern, a 5 by 5 square with a 3 by 3 hole, counted as big square minus hole and as four sides plus corners.
images.composition: One square frame of tiles centred, with two short count labels beside it. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A square frame of square tiles: outer size 5 by 5 tiles, with an empty 3 by 3 hole in the middle drawn with a dashed grey (#6B7280) outline. The 4 corner tiles are amber (#E69F00); the other 12 tiles, 3 on each side, are teal (#0072B2). Exactly 16 tiles. To the right of the frame, stacked: '5 × 5 − 3 × 3 = 16', '4 × 3 + 4 = 16', and below them in reddish purple (#CC79A7) 'Step n: 4n + 4'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: (n + 2)² − n² and 4n + 4 count the same tiles.
images.description: Shows Step 3 of the tile pattern, a 5 by 5 square with a 3 by 3 hole, counted as big square minus hole and as four sides plus corners.
images.context: Steps 1, 2, 3 have 8, 12, 16 tiles; Step 4 has 20, Step 10 has 44; (n + 2)² − n² = 4n + 4.

image_decisions.why: Colouring corners and sides lets both counts be read off the same frame.
